designs.title: Vineyard
designs.why: A strong, sellable composition. The arched window gives the back a clear architectural silhouette, and the S-curves of the terraces pull the eye from the foreground grapes up to the farmhouse and cypresses, so it holds together whole, even from 3 m. At full size the engraving and the fine screen are rich: the leaves, grape bunches and stone walls read cleanly, and the cypresses cropped by the arch look intentional. What keeps it from premium is the typography and the fit to the frame. VINEYARD is a small, widely tracked mono-grotesk that becomes a caption on the shirt, and its rule (about 55% of the arch width) matches neither the word nor the arch. The image also sits inside the keyline unevenly: a white gutter runs down both straight sides, the right side cuts off in a hard vertical edge short of the line, and at the top the trees run into the curve. The midtones are dense and grey overall, with little pure white for air.
designs.fix: Bring the image and the type into one system. Mask the engraving to the arch with one even inset all around (or bleed it to the keyline everywhere), and set VINEYARD about 1.5-2x larger and heavier, with the rule as wide as the arch (or as wide as the word), so the heading reads at the same scale as the window.
